subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron quarantine overflow archives be silently pruned to a fixed count of five, or must recovery records remain available until an explicit cleanup/recovery path is defined?
rationale: The fixed archive limit is a new product policy for persisted recovery evidence, and source-level correctness cannot determine whether deleting older quarantined jobs is acceptable.

options.title: Approve fixed retention
options.body: Accept five retained archive files as the recovery-data contract and merge with that intentional deletion behavior.

options.title: Use non-destructive cleanup
options.body: Keep bounded reads and overflow rotation, but replace silent pruning with a user-visible or doctor-owned cleanup/recovery path.

options.title: Pause the archive design
options.body: Do not merge archive rotation until the cron recovery-retention policy has an owner and explicit acceptance.

recommendation.title: Use non-destructive cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep bounded reads and overflow rotation, but replace silent pruning with a user-visible or doctor-owned cleanup/recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: No reliable current-main feature-history owner could be established from the available read-only evidence.
